strings.translation: Choose a category.
Choose a monster.
Giants
Mythical
Dragons
Animals
Beastfolk
Undead
Demons
Insects
Magical
Mysterious
Warriors
Mages
Thieves
Priests

The runes carved on
its chest mark the
golem-maker's art.
This Stone Golem
was built from
gathered ore. Being
lifeless, a golem has
no fear of pain and
never flinches. A
rather awkward foe
to fight.

A plainly toxic,
misshapen giant. Its
oddly swollen parts
hold gas, and the
deadly poison breath
it vents is a stronger
weapon than sword or
spell. Perhaps due to
its own poison, its
flesh has wasted
away to the bare
minimum.

A silver-white giant
wreathed in cold,
though calling its
shape human is a bit
of a stretch. Its
breath whips up a
blizzard, piling up
the frozen lost in
the maze.

A one-eyed giant of
old legend. In a time
of dire famine he
fused with plants to
survive. His strength
waned, but he rose
again here as a
wholly different
monster. Blessed
with great vitality,
he calmly awaits
adventurers without
a trace of rage.

A giant of flame
with a brown body
like seething magma.
Its searing breath
turns everything
around into a sea of
fire. Beware more
than the flames,
though. Its great
strength is no joke
either.

A giant with no
lower body. It's said
he defied the gods
and was struck down.
Even now his
strength is
frightful. Just how
strong was he back
when he still had
legs?

A golem of fire, made
by cultists in their
god's likeness. Oddly
for a golem, it
attacks with
tentacles and claws.
Its flames are hotter
than any adventurer
has felt. Worse, its
spell resistance is so
high our magic
barely works at all.

A golem of shadow
cast by a strange
statue. Being
antimatter it is hard
to hit, and
adventurers are in
for a tough fight.
The scream from its
shadow tears the
souls of the living
from this world.

The mightiest golem,
built by cultists
pooling all their
wisdom in their god's
likeness. It is
practically a weapon
of war, and ordinary
adventurers stand no
chance. Taking it on
with sword and spell
may well be reckless.

If a wind blows
through the maze
and you suddenly
bleed, the Halycon
may be to blame. A
wind spirit gone mad,
it now delights in
hurting others. Its
bloody scythe marks
a knack for critical
hits, and it reaps
adventurers' heads
like grass.

The name brings a
lizard to mind, but
whatever the shape,
beware of
petrification just
the same. Basilisk is
the general name for
monsters with a
stiffening poison.
Best not to meet its
eyes and get turned
to stone by accident.

A bull-headed man.
Cheap armor means
nothing to him. They
say he splits heads,
helmet and all. His
trophies hang from
his belt, so take care
unless you wish to
join them. If his axe
comes down on your
head, it's all over.

Truly a creature of
myth, found in the
old books. Yet this
one was made by
someone's hand. It is
swift and carries a
longbow, so even the
back row can't relax.
And if you do get
behind it, a fierce
hind kick awaits.

A crocodile monster
said to dwell in hell.
Its huge body gives
adventurers no end of
grief. Such brutes
are usually all
brawn, but sadly this
one can heal itself
too. Add high spell
resistance and you
may as well give up.

A special statue set
in the maze by
the natives of this
land to repel
invaders. Normally
it's just stone, but
once it spots an
intruder it attacks
until the foe is gone.
The rocks it spits
can petrify, making
statues of
adventurers.

Once of divine blood,
her beauty and
bearing have yet to
fade. But now she is
a fearsome monster,
and her petrifying
power is known to
all. Of course, it pays
to watch out for her
snake bites and
poison breath as
well.

An ancient demon
that flies freely
even through skies
beyond our reach. Its
limbs are weapons,
and its sharp claws
shred its prey. A
Hobbit would die in
one blow. Its magic is
strong too, with
Priest and Alchemist
spells.

A guardian of the
Cara Acol temple and
one of the Four
Pillar Gods: the
sacred tiger. Those
who fight it learn
firsthand it's no
ordinary tiger. Still,
its fangs are as
sharp as any wild
tiger's.

A guardian of the
Cara Acol temple and
one of the Four
Pillar Gods: the
sacred dog. It doesn't
seem strong, yet its
solemn air overawes
adventurers. Its bites
and body slams are
worthy of a guardian.

A guardian of the
Cara Acol temple and
one of the Four
Pillar Gods: the
sacred bird. Its eyes
seem to see through
all our thoughts. Its
beak gives
adventurers plenty of
trouble.

A guardian of the
Cara Acol temple and
one of the Four
Pillar Gods: the
sacred serpent. Said
even to understand
speech, once it coils
around an adventurer
it won't let go until
they die. Of the four,
the one to watch
most closely.

The one and only god
of the cultists who
rule this maze. To
them he is water,
sun and creator. He
raises his fists,
casts spells, and his
breath brings
petrification.
Whoever turns a
blade on this god
will soon regret it.

A naked warrior with
a mighty body. It
presses on
unflinching no
matter what hits it,
which startles and
confuses adventurers.
No wonder: the body
is only a puppet. The
bright red mask is
the real monster.

A lost line of dragon.
Get gored by its horn
and it's all over. Its
charge is unmatched.
Never think of
beating it head-on. In
the maze, staying
alive is what
matters, even if it
takes a dirty trick or
two.

The so-called flying
dragon, the best flier
of all dragonkind. But
the maze gives it
little room for that,
making it the easiest
dragon to kill. Still,
an average party will
only end up roasted
by its fire breath.

A green-skinned
dragon of the gas
dragon breed. It
attacks by breathing
out the deadly poison
stored inside it.
Small for a dragon,
but that just means
it's nimble.

A striking dinosaur
with a crest of red
hair on its head. It's
very quick for its
size, and its tail and
claws are hard to
dodge. It has critical
hits and poison, but
it's weak to spells,
and that's the way
through.

A savage meat-eating
dinosaur. Once met, it
will hunt you until
one of you dies. Its
tail strike is brutal
and can land critical
hits. Only a fool
tries to match it
with force.

A dragon that shines
with gold. So grand
and beautiful, it was
worshiped as a god
reborn. It stands
apart even among
dragons, with both
might and high
intellect. Take its
breath full on and
you'll be ash in an
instant.

A dragon said to live
in the flames of hell.
Just meeting one is
something to brag
about. Stand gaping
at it and you'll be
off to the next world
in a flash. It casts no
spells, but its breath
petrifies.

A huge two-headed
dragon. One head
bites its prey while
the other burns it
with fire breath, an
efficient and
fearsome attack. If
you can beat this
dragon, you've earned
some confidence.

A savage, mighty
beast made by a god's
hand. Lacking
intellect, it was
deemed a failure, but
in the maze its
raw power was needed
above all. Its roar
alone will knock the
weak out cold.

A kind of wildcat
native to these parts.
After long years in
the temple, its
hearing is 20 times
sharper than a
normal wildcat's. Its
sight has grown very
poor, and as if to
make up for it, it
has learned a little
magic.

Once an adventurer's
dog, it was left
behind in the
maze and turned
savage. Perhaps it
still longs for
people, for it sidles
up to adventurers and
gently bites them.
Fangs are its main
weapon, but its
breath is strong too.

A bird that flew in
through a temple
window and settled
there, attacking any
creature that came
near to guard its
young. Later, word
spread that its meat
was delicious, and
heartless adventurers
hunted it so hard it
now seldom leaves
the temple.

A two-headed mutant
coyote. Bitten by
both mouths at once,
expect serious
wounds. Otherwise
it's no stronger than
a normal animal, so it
shouldn't give you
much trouble.

It hardly looks like a
rabbit at all. Its two
antennae bristle
with thorns, and it
wraps them around
you like whips.
Beware what comes
next. As you struggle
free, its fangs loom
before your eyes,
aimed at your throat.

An ominous bird
with a skull for a
face. It attacks with
its long beak. It's not
a hard fight, but
meeting one is said
to bring bad luck, so
adventurers hate it.
Just a superstition,
of course.

A lizard that evolved
oddly, though you'd
never guess it from
the way it floats
through the maze.
A sudden bite from
out of nowhere can
cause panic. Watch
out for the venom it
spits from above as
well.

A slug so huge the
squeamish may faint.
Thanks to its body's
makeup, small wounds
close up at once. Best
to kill it without
touching it. If only
there were a spell
that dumped a pile of
salt on it.

A cat that lurks in
the dark and
ambushes its foes.
Its sharp claws and
strong fangs land
critical hit after
critical hit, so
adventurers fear it
as the Blue
Lightning. It's fair
to say it's no mere
animal anymore.

A snake that lived so
long in lightless
caves that its eyes
withered and its skin
hardened. Get coiled
up by a thing like
this and, damage
aside, your nerves
will take a beating
too.

Alligator means
crocodile, but this
one seems to have a
bit of shark in it.
It's faster than you'd
think, and a bite
from that big mouth
means heavy damage.
One is hard enough,
yet it also calls for
help.

A buffalo-like beast
loaded with all the
baggage it can carry.
It charges
adventurers like
that, so you can
guess the damage if
you fail to dodge. A
long fight is trouble,
so use a spell and be
done with it.

A mutant, or
someone's sick
experiment? Either
way, a two-headed
frog. Besides body
slams, it deals
damage with its
croak. Some
adventurers are said
to have cracked from
hearing it too long.
Frog haters, beware.

The largest,
strongest primate. It
has no special
attacks, but its
enormous strength is
a real threat. Even
blocking with a
shield, you'll be sent
flying. Fighting it
without armor is
suicide.

A native riding a
small dragon. Alone
he can barely fight,
but with his dragon
he can match any foe.
His sword and his
dragon's fangs strike
one after the other,
so no wonder it's a
hard fight.

A beast too fierce to
call a dog. Bounding
through the maze, it
looks like a blazing
fire. Indeed, when it
opens its mouth,
searing flames pour
out and roast
adventurers. Maybe
that's why it's red.

Holy places are often
ruled by snakes, and
this twin-headed
serpent has likely
guarded the temple
since ancient times.
Its venom is deadly,
so treat a bite at
once. Worse still, it
can drain levels.

A savage ogre
chained in a prison.
Its strength is
beyond belief. The
iron ball on its chain
doesn't hold it back
at all, it just
becomes a weapon.
Take great care not
to get crushed.

Not a true monkey
but a kind of
lycanthrope. Only
the face is
humanlike, which is
all the stranger. It
swings a club with
its freakishly long
arms. They call
friends and attack in
packs, but which one
is the boss is hard to
tell.

A monster in the
shape of a cute
rabbit. Its staff
holds unimaginable
power: sleep,
paralysis, stun,
poison and special
attacks galore. If
only we could wield
that staff, but no
one has heard of it
being done.

A giant spider
nesting in the
maze. By its shape
it seems to be a
woman, the
spider-woman of
legend perhaps.
Ill-tempered, it
pounces on
adventurers on sight.
At least it has no
poison.

Bats bring vampires
to mind, but this
monster has no tie to
them and doesn't
drink blood at all.
Still, don't let your
guard down. A savage
bat will surely do
adventurers harm.

Scorpions are
dangerous even when
small. What if one
grew as big as us?
This half-man,
half-beast is just
that. Petty tricks
won't scratch its
shell. Before you
know it, its stinger
may lay you low.

Vultures prefer
carrion, but this one
became a beastman
and now attacks the
living too. It strikes
with its beak and
sharp claws. Being
pecked by a flock is
sheer torture. No
wonder some go mad.

A fishman rare even
in the maze. It
favors ice spells, but
it's sure of its fists
too, and it closes in
for melee when it
sees adventurers. A
wise party will have
no trouble, though.
Think about what
beats ice.

A jaguar lycanthrope
that toys with
adventurers with its
quick moves. Its
supple grace seems
feminine, but don't
take it lightly. Its
claws are quite
likely to paralyze.

Its victims, no longer
of this world, can be
seen on its surface.
And if one begs for
help and you lend a
hand, it may turn out
to be the amoeba-man
itself. Nasty
business. It is highly
toxic, so kill it
without touching it
if you can.

A snake monster
flaunting a great
trident. Its skilled
spearwork is like
that of a high-level
Samurai. It can reach
the back row too, so
take care. It's
quicker than you'd
think, slithering in
fast on its writhing
tail.

A humanoid monster
with skin as hard as
an insect's, so it
boasts a high AC
without armor.
Adventurers who
once scorned bugs as
vermin come to
regret it. It has
critical hits, so a
contest of strength
is risky. Spells are
the smart play.

A mad Lord who must
have cast off the
Lord's code long ago.
He looks human, but
think of him as
something else
inside. His beastlike
roar makes every
hair stand on end.
His fierce swordplay
can knock you out
just from blocking
it.

If you hear
something crawling,
look around you. This
monster may be
lurking in the
maze dark. A
centipede beastman
with six arms alone.
Fending off all its
attacks is no easy
feat.

A man dressed as a
clown, out of place in
a maze. His power
is beyond belief, and
his many special
attacks are hard to
resist. Look closely
and it seems
something has taken
human form. Well
known, yet still a
monster shrouded in
mystery.

A spirit gripped by
malice that wanders
this world even after
death. Insubstantial
as a phantom, it
drifts toward the
living to drain their
life force. Many
adventurers can't
stand its shrieking,
so best to Dispel it
quickly.

Once an Alchemist
who brewed magic
potions, now what's
left of one consumed
by their power. It
still attacks with
Alchemist spells. Its
own potions have so
soaked its body that
it hasn't noticed it's
dead, and it keeps
mixing them to this
day.

Not local corpses
risen again, but
would-be conquerors
cursed after death
and put to work as
slaves. They're slow,
but being surrounded
is dangerous, as their
claws and teeth can
paralyze and poison.

Skeletal soldiers
raised by a sorcerer's
curse. They attack
with long spears.
Trading blows with
bodies that are
mostly gaps is a
losing game. A
Priest's Dispel
should work well, and
no doubt their souls
wish for it too.

A creature that
creeps up under cover
of darkness. It lurks
in adventurers'
shadows and strikes
with huge pincers,
more intent on
draining life than
fighting. Its true
nature is still
unclear, but one
thing is known: it
will drain levels.

A bloodsucker, in
short. Unlike a
Zombie, it is
intelligent and adept
with spells. Loathing
sunlight, it dwells in
dim caves. Being
undead, it shrugs off
minor wounds and
presses relentlessly
on to drink
adventurers' blood.

Undead rumored to
have been a king in
life. Whether that's
true is uncertain,
but its power is
truly kingly. It is
skilled in both blows
and magic, and its
energy drain and
other special attacks
can't be ignored. A
formidable foe
without doubt.

The soul of a woman
driven mad by losing
her lover. Finding an
adventurer like him,
she draws near and
sobs forlornly. Ask
after her and she
touches your cheek
with a cold palm,
stealing your life
force. Will the life
she gathers one day
revive her lover?

She adorns herself
with flowers, a habit
from life she can't
shake, perhaps. A
female undead whose
ill-suited body stirs
pity. Every rose has
thorns, they say, but
hers are far worse.
Her long, sharp
claws rend
adventurers and
paralyze them.

Does fear outlast
death? These beings
wear looks of terror.
Several souls mingle
within them, and
given the chance
they attack to draw
adventurers into
their ranks. To us,
this creature's very
existence is fear
itself.

An undead cloaked in
a crimson robe. Its
spellcasting suggests
it was a Mage in life.
Undeath has greatly
raised its magic
power, making it an
even worse threat to
adventurers. Beware
its paralysis and
level drain.

Claw in its right
hand, its own head in
its left, it is undead
born of a guilty
conscience made
flesh. What its form
means is hard to
guess, but forcing
the same look on
adventurers is
nothing but a
nuisance.

A violinist from
Hell. The tones he
plays surely eat away
at adventurers' lives.
His instrument, too,
seems to be alive like
a monster. If you
hear eerie music deep
in the maze, be ready
for the worst.

A misshapen being
that scatters flames
as it attacks. The
heads it bears are
said to be those of
adventurers found
lying in the maze.
The screams from its
mouths drive
listeners mad. Not
how anyone wants to
spend a second life.

Evil spirits are
hardly rare in the
maze, but one this
dangerous is another
matter. It isn't one
being but a chain of
many dead souls. It
casts spells and,
worst of all, even
drains levels.

Undead king who
rules the land of the
dead. Its vivid
feathered headdress
only adds to the
eeriness. Its piercing
glare, its cries, its
outstretched hand all
send you to the
underworld. Even if
you cling to this
world, energy drain
is unavoidable.

A legendary Vampire,
once an ordinary
woman who drank
human blood to
prolong her life and
became undead. Her
fine, pale features
will never fade, built
as they are on the
sacrifice of
adventurers.

A man known as 'the
one alone'. Perhaps
his hood hides a
life-support device,
yet the face beneath
carries an air of
loneliness. For what
purpose, none can
say, but his level
drain steals
adventurers' life
force.

The one who stands
at the peak of the
undead. His graceful
bearing has an air of
nobility. His
overwhelming might
is widely known, and
adventurers and even
lesser monsters
tremble at his name.
Half-hearted attacks
won't leave a scratch.

The Dullahan is a
herald of death. For
adventurers, fighting
him means death.
Headless, he drives a
two-wheeled chariot
called the Coiste
Bodhar straight at
them. Landing a blow
on him is difficult.

The mightiest
familiar, made by a
high demon. Its
unique body is said
to be built from the
bones of every kind
of creature. It wields
four huge scythes,
and one slip can cost
your head. Its skull
face's scream lures
you toward death.

An undead dragon.
Zombified, it can no
longer breathe fire
and instead spews a
deadly poison breath.
It also has spells and
level drain, making it
far more troublesome
than an ordinary
dragon.

Called an ancient
demon god by some, a
king of the undead
by others, and once
even a phoenix, it
seems. Its true
nature is unclear,
but it's doubtful
anyone who met it in
the maze came back
alive. The wind of its
wings brings certain
death.

Don't scorn it as a
mere demon's corpse.
It is a menace denied
even a return to the
netherworld. Spells
barely work on it,
and Dispelling it
looks near impossible.
Some adventurers go
mad at the mere
sight of it.

A ghost famous
among adventurers.
Its AC is low and it's
durable, but its high
experience makes it a
rite of passage for
mid-level
adventurers, who
even speak of him
fondly. For him,
being slain over and
over, it's no fun at
all.

A zombie that guards
golden armor. It
body-slams foes as if
to show off the
armor's strength. The
zombie itself has
little power. It looks
a bit cramped in
there, so put it out
of its misery.

A zombie that guards
golden gauntlets,
though it seems less
to guard them than
to enjoy their power.
The sword in its
hand can deal critical
hits, so deal with it
before someone dies.

A zombie that guards
golden boots. It uses
the boots as weapons,
kicking at
adventurers. Its
blows can paralyze,
so finish it off
before things get
messy.

A zombie that guards
a golden helm, and
puts it to use with
headbutts. Of course
that won't break the
helm, but you'll want
to free it from its
duty as soon as you
can.

An undead warrior
built from bones,
many of them from
adventurers who died
in the maze. Perhaps
from the grudges of
the dead, it shows
uncanny strength,
though turning it on
adventurers seems a
bit misplaced.

Now a mere mummy,
robbed of what it
guarded and left with
no mission. Still, it
shows no mercy, and
its eyes plainly burn
with hostility. It
attacks with a
zombie's usual claws
and bites. Beware
poison and paralysis.

A kind of lesser
demon whose body is
made of smoke, so
swords barely harm
it. Best to attack
with spells before it
calls for help.

From afar they look
like children, but no
ordinary child would
be in a place like
this. Children they
are, but demon
children. They attack
in packs with
strange shears and
chain-sickles.

If you have bad
dreams while resting
in the maze, this
dream demon is to
blame. It loves
nothing more than
giving adventurers
nightmares and
watching their
terror. Awake, the
odd dance it does in
battle is infuriating
to watch.

A servant of demons,
so wickedly beautiful
that the smitten
have carved it into
statues. The Gargoyle
seems to know it, and
sometimes stands
still posing as a
statue, then suddenly
attacks when
adventurers come
close.

A demon one rank up
that blocks
adventurers' way. Its
textbook demonic
form terrifies all
who see it, but if
you can't beat it,
you'll never go
deeper in the maze.
Strong in body and
magic alike, yet it
still calls for help
again and again.

A bat from Hell with
a sickle in each hand.
Unlike other bats it
doesn't drink blood
itself, but its sickles
drip plenty. Take
care unless you want
to fall prey to its
critical hits.

The Succubus is the
famous dream demon,
but this is the male
version. It enters
women's dreams,
shows them lewd
visions and drains
their vitality. Some
male adventurers are
oddly let down on
meeting an Incubus
and attack it with a
vengeance.

A demon famous in
certain circles. Those
she bewitches drown
in indescribable
pleasure by night.
Many adventurers
hope to meet her
someday, but the
weak-willed had best
run.

A monster that truly
fits the name Beast,
its long horns only
adding to it. Hugely
strong, it strikes
hard even without
weapons. It often
appears with Beauty,
so adventurers call
them 'Beauty and the
Beast'.

A rock demon bearing
the fires of Hell.
When it appears, the
maze grows
noticeably hotter,
and its attacks are
scalding too. Its
weakness is naturally
cold, but weak
attacks are just
water on a hot stone.

A grand name,
'Master of Hell', but
its rank in the
netherworld isn't
that high. Its power,
of course, rivals any
demon's. Its whip is
made of countless
spines, and if it
breaks, it just finds
new ones. The maze is
full of adventurers,
after all.

A huge gatekeeper of
Hell who bars
adventurers' way, a
demon who sees us as
little more than
game to hunt. Its
long staff is said to
be made from
adventurers' bones. It
knows spells, but
mostly uses them for
slaughter.

Hell's ripper, carving
up all it sees. It
looks like an animal,
but it's one of the
greater demons. Quick
for its bulk, it goes
for critical hits. As
its looks suggest,
it's very tough.

A cruel demon that
loves to fight, and
its face plainly
shows it enjoys
slaughter. Its power
is immense, and a
direct hit can knock
you out. Resistant to
spells and able to
heal itself, it's a
tough foe. If you
meet it, brace
yourself.

A towering demon
that overwhelms all
who see it. Its hide,
hard as natural
armor, shrugs off
most attacks, while
its mighty claws
pierce adventurers'
armor. Spells are all
but useless on it.
That they come in
groups is another
headache.

This monster is made
wholly of substances
harmful to normal
living things. To
adventurers, that
means poison and
paralysis. So a stab
from its long claws
to a vital spot means
instant death.

A demon that spreads
plague across the
land. Where it
passes, it leaves
mountains of corpses.
Stopping it at the
source would be ideal,
but it's no easy
matter. You're more
likely to die before
the plague even gets
you.

A huge demon whose
body stretches in
many folds. It hides
its many tentacles
underground and
strikes from every
direction. Some even
say earthquakes are
its doing. Its magic
is bottomless, and it
can supposedly cast
every spell we know.

A demon with all
knowledge, able to
fulfill every desire.
To it, the magic we
use is mere child's
play. Its bizarre body
is said to take in the
strengths of many
creatures. It is far
beyond our reach.

A demon that brings
misfortune wherever
it goes. Famine and
other disasters are
said to be its work
too. For adventurers,
misfortune takes the
simplest form: death.

A noble of the
netherworld, of sorts.
It looks much like a
Human, but goat
horns give it away.
This clever demon
has great magic
power and wields
both Priest and Mage
spells, plus strong
special attacks such
as petrifying and
critical hits.

A demonic beast with
great wings. Its
might is far beyond
any animal, and a
blow from its tail
lands like a falling
axe. It can also
petrify, and its
victims then become
its meal.

Monarch of the
netherworld, ruler of
demons. The
intelligent visage
glimpsed in its huge
form captivates all
who see it. Or
perhaps 'freezes in
fear' is closer.
Wielding hellfire and
a huge axe, it snuffs
out adventurers'
lives in an instant.

This monster had no
name at first. 'Hims'
comes from between
'him' and 'them',
since even one of it
is as strong as a
whole pack of
monsters. The god
who made 'them' so
feared their power it
sealed them deep
underground.

A demon infant fresh
from its egg, in
truth a lab creature
made by heretics. Its
still-clumsy breath
can put you to sleep.
Best to slay it before
it grows up.

An ordinary ant from
a far-off land that
stowed away in an
adventurer's pack and
grew huge in Lake
Cara's waters. Alone
it's weak, but it
swarms, making it a
nuisance. It's so
hardy no one's heard
of insecticide wiping
it out.

A giant mosquito. It
flies at adventurers'
wounds to drink blood
and lay eggs. Most
never notice until
the scab falls off and
larvae hatch out.
Insecticide is useless
on it, and one
sometimes causes an
uproar at the inn.

A local beetle with a
very hard shell.
Punching it
barehanded is
honestly not advised.
Some careless souls
have been run
through by its horn,
leather armor and all.
Airborne, it flies
like an arrow, so kill
it before it takes off.

A spider that fools
adventurers by
posing as a pillar in
the ruins. Beyond
mere mimicry, even
its body is hard as
stone, which is
rather impressive.
Some adventurers
never suspect a
thing and lean on it
to rest.

An ancient breed of
fly. Fierce and keen
of smell, it follows
the scent of blood. It
fights with sharp
claws and a tail, and
true to its name it
has a breath attack
too. It never lands, so
hitting it is quite a
chore.

Who looked at this
and called it a bat?
True, it strikes from
the dark and leaves
wounds like fang
marks, so the idea is
fair. Only recently
did its secret come
out. No one guessed
those wounds came
from its forked tail.

A bizarre dragonfly
with a human face,
said to be a Faerie in
truth. Weak in
attack and defense,
it's no real threat,
but in numbers it
gets a bit annoying.
Best to clear them
out with a spell.

A hateful monster of
a mosquito. A normal
mosquito bite is bad
enough, but this one
may take your life
along with your
blood. At least
something this big
is hard to lose sight
of. Kill it before it
stings you.

A crab monster with
huge pincers. Its
shell is hard but its
stamina low, so only
novices should
struggle. As one look
will tell you, beware
critical hits from
those pincers. Crabs
are for eating, not
for being eaten by.

A bizarre caterpillar
with a human face
that crawls all over
the maze. Meet its
eyes as you go to
stomp it and you may
hesitate. Squash it
anyway and it
splatters fluids
everywhere, which is
most unpleasant.

So big and strange it
hardly counts as a
mantis. Luckily its
wings have withered,
so it can't fly. A
cannibal breed to
begin with, it grew
even more vicious as
it grew huge. Beware
critical hits from its
giant scythes.

A chimera of
mushroom and leech.
The mushroom's
spores sting bare
skin, while the leech
latches onto
adventurers to drain
their blood. It's small
enough to kill by
stepping on it, and
the squelch is quite
satisfying.

A man-eating plant,
though it usually
sticks to feeding on
carcasses.
Adventurers who
show up during its
meal draw its wrath
and are lashed with
tentacles. Still, it's
only a plant, and a
fire spell should
reduce it to ash.

A ball of the maze's
dust and mold, said to
hold a dead man's
soul at its core. Its
attacks are next to
harmless, but it
keeps calling more of
its kind, so the fight
will drag on. It gives
little experience too,
making it a real pest.

A flytrap eats flies,
but this is that
plant grown huge. A
bigger body means a
bigger appetite, and
it seems to have
acquired a taste for
adventurers. It wraps
its tendrils around
prey to pull it in.
Being a plant, it
burns well with fire
spells.

An odd monster that
startles adventurers
by suddenly flipping
its head open.
Breathe in the smoke
that spews out and
you may go insane.
Beyond that it has
no real powers.
Scaring people is all
it has in its head.

Its strange dance,
which may make you
forget to attack, is
worth seeing once.
Watch it too often,
though, and you'll
need more lives than
you have. They
attack in groups, so
strike them all down
at once with spells.

Creepy as it looks,
it's apparently a kind
of frog. Its slimy
body, as if melted
into the floor,
disgusts all who see
it. Its breath is oddly
sweet, but it brings
sleep. It can heal
itself too, so it may
prove tougher than
expected.

The statue of a
foreign noble given
life, in other words a
kind of golem. Being
made of stone, it hits
very hard, and its
kicks and punches
are shockingly heavy.
If it began as a
statue, there must
have been a noble
who posed for it.

An automaton made
by persons unknown.
Only its face came
from a living thing,
which makes it all
the more grotesque.
Mostly wood, it looks
flimsy but is quite
sturdy. It charges at
adventurers with a
hammer arm and a
dagger arm.

A monster whose
right arm is itself a
syringe. The fluid
inside seems to flow
straight from its
own body, and it
contains poison. It
lunges at
adventurers, trying
to stab its needle
into them.

A very rare liquid
creature. Look closely
and you'll see it's
made of pooled blood,
so its fluid attack
means a dousing in
blood. Blood draws
more blood and
spawns more of its
kind. Perhaps the
blood you've shed is
part of them too.

A liquid creature you
can stab or stomp
without feeling a
thing. It attacks
with tentacles and
fluids, with poison
and paralysis thrown
in, so no wonder
adventurers hate it.
Once it calls friends,
the area fills with
Blobs and there's no
room left to stand.

A truly strange
sight. A man in a
painting floating in
midair stares right
at you. But beware.
Get too close and the
man spits out
strange creatures
that wrap around
you. Before you know
it, you may become a
resident of the
painting yourself.

A monster named for
its sharp fangs,
which it uses to
bite. The claws on its
forelegs are strong
too, and if you drop
your guard you'll fall
prey to a critical hit.
Tentacles grafted
onto its back have
widened its range of
attacks even further.

A shape that makes
you want to look
away. Its face and
limbs are horribly
misshapen, and its
body, with the
organs showing
through, was plainly
made by someone.
Even adventurers
don't like to say
much about this
monster.

Frankly, no one
knows quite what
this creature is. It
seems a being of gas,
yet adventurers who
met it swear it bit
them. It casts
Psionic spells, which
hints at a being of
pure mind. Either
way, it's an eerie
monster.

What's left of an
adventurer used as
someone's test
subject. The
experiment didn't
exactly fail, but it
ruined his mind, and
now he attacks
anyone who comes
near. A tragic soul
who became no
different from a
monster.

Inside is a Demon
Imp. It isn't being
protected, it's being
drained of nutrients.
The mushroom is the
real monster, a
parasite. Not even its
fellow Demon Imps
will help it, since if
caught they'd suffer
the same fate.

A gaseous monster
shaped like many
animals, whose fangs
and claws go straight
for adventurers. It's
little more than
mist, yet it casts
spells and even heals.
Get caught in its
breath and you'll
drift into a pleasant
sleep.

A Blob grown huge.
Blobs are a nuisance
to begin with, and
one this big is even
harder to get rid of.
What you once
stomped on may now
stomp on you. Worse
yet, this Blob has a
petrifying attack.

A carnivorous plant
bred as a living trap
for adventurers. Its
many tendrils snare
them and toss them
one by one into the
petals at its center,
which serve as its
mouth. Its many
blossoms look like a
hydra's heads, hence
the name.

A strange creature
made from the bodies
of many animals,
with two old women's
faces at its center.
Their chants and
breath lull
adventurers into deep
sleep. The dreams are
surely nightmares,
and with bad luck
that sleep lasts
forever.

A fire spirit that
lights the dark maze,
so stately that some
who meet it mistake
it for a priest. Its
arms, long as
tentacles, hold their
catch until it burns
away. It's weak to
fire's opposite, but
that's useless
without the power to
exploit it.

Countless eyes bulge
from its amoeba-like
body. Just being
glared at by them
does damage, and the
worst cases end up
paralyzed or insane.
Even today it lurks
deep in the maze,
watching
adventurers.

Surely it's bliss to
live surrounded by
the things you love.
This one loves the
cold so much that it
covers its body in
ice. For it, the ice
itself is both weapon
and armor. Naturally,
the breath it exhales
is freezing cold.

A thick gas that
suddenly appears in
the maze is surely a
Gas Cloud. It isn't
natural but a
guardian made by
cultists. Caught in
its smoke, you'll be
overcome by sleep
you can't resist.
Somehow, it even
casts spells.

A small being born
of a machine. Never
judge a foe by its
size alone, for that
little body hides
untold power. If you
can't spot it, you'll
be hit without
knowing what's
happening.

A chimera warrior
fused from many
creatures. Three
adventurers can be
seen trapped in its
middle. Built for
combat, it is a
synthetic creature
made by cultists.

A creature born of
the cultists'
experiments and,
sadly, deemed a
failure. It seems to
beg for help, but
lend it a hand and
you'll learn firsthand
that it's already too
late. The kind thing
is to put it out of
its misery quickly.

All sorts of rubbish
turns up in the
maze: dust, rusted
weapons, carcasses,
and the restless
souls of those who
died with regrets.
All of it came
together to form
this monster, which
attacks adventurers
to make them part of
itself.

A new guardian made
by cultists with the
maze's lore and
machines. So little
flesh remains that it
hardly counts as a
living thing. Its
pale, translucent face
never changes as it
carries out its orders.
Its sharp claws cause
poison and paralysis.

No true angel would
be found in a place
like this. As its
name says, it is a
fake, a fool posing as
an angel. Look
closely: its angelic
wings are a machine
on its back, and it
holds a hooked claw
on a cord.

By rights, this was
meant to be an angel.
It is a botched one,
as if a god had
stopped halfway
through making it.
Too weak even to
fall from grace, it
does little more than
harass adventurers
in the maze. A truly
puzzling creature.

A fallen angel in a
skull mask. It must
hide what it is, for
if that were known,
it is said, disaster
would follow, enough
to swap Heaven and
Hell. Its power shows
both angel and
demon, and the bloody
blades in its hands
have slain many.

A guardian of the
cultists' treasury. Its
mineral body is
astonishingly hard.
In the right light it
might pass for a gem
itself, but who
wants a gem with a
face and arms?

A demon race a bit
smaller than Humans,
cruel, savage and
hideous of face. The
Goblin can never
make peace with
Humans, and attacks
on sight without a
word. Its attacks are
simple, though, and
it's no great threat.

A race of dogs that
walk on two legs.
Small but aggressive,
the Kobold falls on
anything like a
starving stray.
Neither its wits nor
its brawn amount to
much, though. At
least it bothers to
wear armor.

A pig-faced
humanoid, vicious and
greedy, forever
pillaging. Orcs are
foes not only of
Humans but of Elves
and Dwarves as well.
They look tougher
than Goblins or
Kobolds, but there
isn't much
difference.

A demon race smaller
still than Goblins.
Proper gremlins get
up to nothing worse
than petty mischief,
but this Gremlin is
far more vicious,
running rings around
adventurers. With
that build, though,
it's no Fighter. Thief
would suit it better,
surely.

A cultist warrior
who stakes all for
his god. Simple,
perhaps, but such
men are the truly
fearsome ones. Meet
him head-on or trip
him up with magic,
as you like. Just
don't get cocky and
have your skull split
by his iron ball.

A man-eater, said to
rule over the other
demon races. The
Ogre is crude and
cruel beyond measure,
and its huge body
gives its blows a
strength not to be
taken lightly. It's
short on brains,
though, so a little
cunning will see it
off.

The elite of the
Gremlin race. Braver
than the rest, it
takes up a weapon
and charges straight
in. A fine spirit
indeed, but attacking
is all it knows how
to do.

Captain of the Orc
vanguard, he charges
boldly in with cape
streaming. So nimble
you'd hardly take
him for an Orc.
Frankly, he's a tough
foe, and you're in for
a hard fight.

A wrecker who
merely borrows the
name of Fighter.
With a great
sledgehammer and a
buzz saw for an arm,
he smashes all he
sees. Only while
destroying does he
feel true joy, they
say. Try not to
become his next
target.

A berserker
enthralled by a mask.
Its wearer kills
without end, craving
blood as red as the
mask, freed only
when his own life
ends. Even once this
one's task is done, a
new berserker will
someday liven up the
maze.

This, surely, is what
an Ogre was meant to
be: bulging muscles
and crimson skin, a
true red demon. He
puts that strength
to use as a Monk, so
beware his Psionic
spells as well.

A Fighter in name
only, and a vile
sadist who'll go to
any lengths to
torture a foe. Indeed,
his victims die not
in battle but under
the torture after. In
a way he's worse
than a monster that
knows no speech.

Body and soul, he has
given himself to his
god. A formidable
cultist Lord, and well
equipped too. Should
you face a party that
includes him, it's
plain as day you're in
for a hard fight.

A bigger breed of
Goblin, with
abilities to match its
size. Its wits are no
better, though, and
it simply shoves
forward unarmed
with brute force.
You're under no
obligation to take it
head-on, so use
spells.

A prince must
outrank the other
Goblins. Indeed, he's
a Lord, with the
abilities and gear to
match. Best to think
of him as a different
creature altogether
from the common
Goblin.

Leader of the
Kobolds, with
abilities far beyond
the common Kobold.
As a Lord he casts
Priest spells. His
stately guard shows
not a single opening,
and his sword will
surely carve
adventurers to pieces.

Of the Orcs' ruling
class stands the Orc
Lord. With his
leadership and
healing, an Orc party
becomes a much
tougher foe. Take
extra care whenever
he is among them.

In the East, a daimyo
is a leader of
Samurai. Odd, then,
to see an Ogre in the
role, but judging by
his arms and armor
he has fully
embraced it. He has
the skill to back it
up, too, and is a
formidable foe.

A Monk of high rank
who uses no magic
and trusts only his
own body. Feeble
adventurers feel
worn away by his
aura alone. Sheathed
in armor of muscle,
he shrugs off even
swords. Don't hold
back: use magic and
items.

A Knight of
Diamonds summoned
from another world.
His gear, known as
the K.O.D.'s items, is
of noble pedigree
there. Superb in
attack and defense
alike, he fights with
an almost divine
grace. As an ally,
none could be more
reassuring.

A dragon knight who
defies all reason,
with a dragon's full
might and the rank
of Lord besides. His
stats are high across
the board, his
vitality bottomless.
He has every special
ability, and his holy
breath brings death
to all alike.

A Mage of striking
beauty. No wonder
adventurers drop
their guard. But pick
a fight lightly and
you'll pay dearly.
She's scantily clad,
yet her Armor Class
is remarkably low.

What becomes of the
brighter Orcs after
long study of magic.
Its power rivals an
Elf or Gnome
Priest's, and it will
torment adventurers.
Silencing it early is
the key.

Gremlins may be
more versatile than
we imagine. This one
is quite aged, yet has
mastered Mage
spells, and up close
her claws, her true
weapons, will rend
you. Mothers are
strong, it seems.

A four-armed Goblin
bearing the title
Oracle, and big for a
Goblin. Might its
Psionic spells have
to do with its form?
Handy, at least, that
its free hands can
strike back even
mid-chant.

A Psionic, and very
rare among
dim-witted Orcs. It is
said to be born of
mutation. Its killing
intent becomes a dark
force that wounds
adventurers one after
another.

An Ogre Mage who
hardly plays to his
strengths. Still,
adventurers may
count themselves
lucky that an Ogre's
vaunted might isn't
going into his blows.
The snake coiled
around him is his
beloved pet, it seems.

A cultist Mage
whose great power is
plain at a glance. His
look, every bit the
evil wizard, cows
adventurers. Reason
says his vitality
should be low, so
attack without
flinching. If he gets
his spells off, you're
in trouble.

A Goblin of the
shaman's rank, its
painted markings
heightening its air
of sorcery. Among
Goblins, using magic
must carry real
status. Up close it
attacks with claws
and fists, but in
melee the upper hand
is yours.

The things you see
around him are no
illusion. He can give
his aura solid form
and hurl it at
adventurers, which
is hard to bear. His
mind is a bit
unhinged.

When the old man
scatters ash, chaos
breaks out in the
maze. The ash blinds,
and he casts spells
meanwhile, an
efficient tactic.
Don't underestimate
an old man's wisdom.

Does it strike the
mind directly? Once
you're in its sight,
damage piles up for
no clear reason. Meet
its gaze and things
get worse. The weak
of mind can't even
touch it.

She is as lovely as
her name, but the
fairest flower has
thorns: she comes at
adventurers with a
hidden dagger.
Usually found with
Human parties, but
sometimes with
monsters too.

To a Kobold, hunting
is life itself. The
bow is no mere tool
but a vital weapon
for survival, and
failing to master it
means death. Facing
adventurers with
such resolve, no
wonder it's a hard
fight.

Decked out in black,
yet a Goblin Ninja
just looks awkward.
Even so, his skills
are truly a Ninja's.
He knows spells as
well. For a Goblin, he
must have trained
hard indeed.

A cunning
two-headed thief.
Violent by nature,
even its two heads
don't get along and
are forever
quarreling. Only in
front of a foe do
they cooperate,
hounding adventurers
with superb
teamwork.

Each beat of his
drum shaves away an
adventurer's life.
Listening unguarded
is suicide. He casts
Mage spells too, so
bring him down
quickly.

A typical Hobbit
Thief. Cute face, but
already a grown adult
as Hobbits go. He
hates being treated
like a child, and
when he senses it he
attacks in a huff.
Truly,
underestimating him
is dangerous.

A highly mobile
female Ranger who
hates keeping still,
always watching for
a chance to attack.
She's quite sure of
her bow and dagger.
Nothing pleases her
more than cutting up
male adventurers who
underestimate her.

Given Kobold habits,
the thief's trade may
have suited them
from the start. Quick
as a starving stray,
it gleefully leaps on
any prey it finds. Its
basic abilities are
low, so if it's a
bother, drive it off
with spells.

A fearsome killing
machine creeping
from the dark: that's
a Ninja. Don't relax
just because he's
unarmed. His whole
body is a weapon.
Before you know it,
your party could be
wiped out.

The Sylph, said to be
a wind spirit. Having
one as your party's
Priest would be
reassuring. But she's
a priestess of the
cult, on a side that
can never understand
ours. You must defend
yourself, of course,
but you'd rather not
meet her as a foe.

Who'd have dreamed
such an odd Gremlin
existed? And a
Bishop, no less. To
make up for its lack
of ability, it puts
three heads' worth
of brains to work.
Unless you seal its
spells, a hard fight
is certain.

That Kobolds have
priests shows they
do have a culture,
oddly enough. Even
for a Kobold, its
solemn bearing is
quite something. It's
still an enemy of
adventurers, of
course, so enough
praise.

A cultist Priest who
worships a god other
than ours. Yet it's
far too sinister to
call a priest. It has
more of a Monk's air
about it, and its
blows land hard.
Return the favor and
thrash it without
holding back.

It's no wonder guards
slip before her
beauty. Many
adventurers seem
charmed before she
casts a spell. But
don't forget, she's a
cultist Priest. Stand
there gaping and her
attacks will show no
mercy.

Once they become
Bishops, you can no
longer scoff at mere
Goblins. In battle
you'd want its spells
sealed, but if it acts
first it's a sorry
sight. The staff it
holds hides some
special power.

A healer is one who
heals, and as the
name says, it's a
Priest. Finding one
among Orcs, who live
for pillage and ruin,
is a surprise. Being
an Orc, it's handy
with blows too. Orc
priests sure look
rough, though.

A spell master who
has learned every
spell. Against the
unskilled, a glance
alone does damage, no
spell needed. Yet at
his great age, he
prolongs his life
with a strange
fluid-filled machine.
Even a master of
magic can't beat old
age, it seems.

A cultist Bishop
devoted to his god
through long
training. Even if
you're lucky enough
to seal his spells, a
parade of special
attacks awaits.
Galling as it is,
perhaps 'sage' is the
word for such a one.
